correctness.rationale: On the quotient of vertex functions by constants, leaf-to-hub gradient g in R^k maps as B_alpha g=[alpha I-(1-alpha)Q]g with Q=11^T/k. Orthogonal idempotents give B^m=a(I-Q)+bQ, a=alpha^m, b=(2alpha-1)^m. Its induced edge-TV norm equals the common l1 column sum [|(k-1)a+b|+(k-1)|b-a|]/k, algebraically equal to max(|b|,[2(k-1)a-(k-2)b]/k), and leaf-indicator gradients attain it. On alpha>=1/2 the active branch strictly increases. For even m the contracting |1-2alpha|^m branch crosses at 1/3 and then the other strictly increases; at 1/3 B^m=3^{-m}I exactly. For odd m, the cusp alpha0=1/[2+(k-1)^(1/m)] competes with the F derivative, whose positive/negative sign produces unique cusp at k=2,3 and unique interior stationary optimum at k>=4 for m>=3. Direct rational independent iterations corroborated 320 parameter cases with k=2,3,4,6,m=1..5 and alpha=j/15.
residual_risks: The numerical optimization grid in source cannot itself prove uniqueness; the analytical derivative sign proof does. Conditions require fixed alpha across all m steps and unweighted edge J.
